note: The Cypress specs, packed into balanced shards for CI. One GitHub Actions
runner per shard, each booting its own API + frontend.
The packing is derived from measured per-spec durations — see
E2E_PERFORMANCE_PLAN.md § 1 for the table and how to refresh it. Do NOT
split alphabetically or by file count: filters.cy.ts and
manufacturer_api_docs.cy.ts are ~125x apart, and the job is only as fast as
its slowest shard. `estimate` is the pre-sharding cost of that shard's
specs, kept here so the balance is reviewable in a diff.
REPACKED when table.cy.ts landed. At 5:23 it is the second longest spec in
the suite, and every shard was already ~6:00, so there was no headroom
anywhere to drop it into: on the smallest it made that runner 11:14 and the
whole job with it. The 22 specs that have CI numbers are packed longest-first
from that table; filters.cy.ts is no longer alone on a runner, which is why
tests/unit/shards.test.ts stopped hardcoding that.
table.cy.ts was 5:23 when this was packed and measures 4:13 since the
compare selection stopped writing the URL — a LOCAL number either way, and
manuals/brand_filter/co_listings are still residuals — refresh all four from
the next green run. The packing is only as good as those four numbers.
admin_triage and submissions stay in DIFFERENT shards on purpose: they share
one API process per runner, and the triage queue is one page of the oldest
50 pending rows, so a spec that files submissions first can push the
fixtures triage looks for off the page (CLAUDE.md § Commands).
EVERY spec in cypress/e2e/ must appear in exactly one shard. A spec left out
would silently stop running while CI stayed green, so
scripts/check-shards.mjs enforces it — run by `npm run test:unit` and by
CI's shard-planning job. Adding a spec means adding it here.
